note: Rules, as data. DESIGN.md 5. The engine that reads these is src/engine/rules.ts
and it contains no rule of its own.
Every rule carries a `say`, and the validator fails the build without one:
the surface renders the sentence and never the number, so a score that
cannot explain itself is a score nobody should trust.
`source` says where a rule comes from and the three values are not equal.
`source` means it traces to a named symbol in the game's Lua and is a fact.
`wiki` is a lead somebody verified. `curator` is a judgement, and the owner's
to make. Nothing here is `curator` yet, because every rule below is derived
from the game's own tables rather than from an opinion about what is good.
npm run health measures each one against 300 random legal runs and flags
anything firing on 60 percent or more of its eligible pool. A rule that
fires on everything says nothing. Run it before adding the next one.
knownGaps: No rule here judges whether a boon is good. That is the owner's and it is in no file.

free-of-the-cap cannot be measured by npm run health: runsim draws Olympian Exits only, so Hermes, Selene and Chaos never appear in a simulated offer even though they are three of the eighteen slots in RewardStoreData.RunProgress. Extend the simulator before trusting its number.
Nothing reads data/generated/stacking.json yet. A rule keyed on a boon already at its diminishing point wants it, and the 20 curves are sitting there.
No rule knows what a boon does. That needs the curated feeds tag, DESIGN.md 12 item 8, which the briefing's centre of mass is also waiting on.

records.say: This is the last piece of {target}.
records.why: DESIGN.md 5 names this as the rule coupling the two engines. Fires on 32% of offers.

records.say: {target} is running out of Exits, and this is one of the pieces.
records.why: Fires on 3% of offers. AT_RISK is rare until a run is nearly over, which is the point.

records.say: Heroic is the top of the ladder, so this shuts its slot for the rest of the run.
records.why: TraitRarityData.RarityUpgradeOrder ends at Heroic and GetReplacementTraits only offers a swap while the held boon can still be upgraded. Fires on 3% of offers.

records.say: Taking this spends one of your four Olympian slots on a new god.
records.why: HeroData.MaxGodsPerRun, counted by ReachedMaxGods over loot carrying GodLoot. Fires on 30% of offers, which is roughly how often a new god is behind an Exit.

records.say: Costs no Olympian slot: the cap counts only loot carrying GodLoot.
records.why: LootData.BaseLoot gives GodLoot true by inheritance and these three do not carry it. Unmeasured, see knownGaps.
